lessons.title: Mixtures: Weighted Average Concept
lessons.concept: When two or more quantities are mixed, the overall value (such as price, concentration, or average) is the weighted average based on their amounts. If quantities q1,q2 with values v1,v2 are mixed, mean value = (q1*v1 + q2*v2)/(q1+q2).
lessons.formula: Mean value = (sum of quantity×value) / (sum of quantities).
mistakes: Taking simple average instead of weighted average when quantities differ
Adding values without weighting by quantities
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Alligation Rule
lessons.concept: Alligation is a shortcut to find the ratio in which two ingredients with different values must be mixed to obtain a mixture of a given mean value. Place cheaper value (C), mean (M), dearer (D) and take differences diagonally: ratio (quantity of cheaper):(quantity of dearer) = (D-M):(M-C).
lessons.formula: If C < M < D, ratio C:D = (D - M) : (M - C).
lessons.worked_example: Mix items at ₹20/kg and ₹50/kg to get ₹30/kg. Ratio = (50-30):(30-20) = 20:10 = 2:1 (cheaper:dearer).
mistakes: Placing mean outside the range of the two values (impossible for simple mixture)
Subtracting in wrong order and getting negative/incorrect ratio
Swapping which difference corresponds to which ingredient
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Replacement in Mixtures
lessons.concept: In replacement problems, a part of a mixture is removed and replaced by another substance (often water). After each operation, the fraction of the original substance remaining is multiplied by (1 - removed/total). For n operations with same quantity replaced: remaining original = V*(1 - r/V)^n.
lessons.formula: Remaining quantity of original = Initial * (1 - replaced_amount/total_volume)^n.
lessons.worked_example: A 20 L vessel full of milk: remove 5 L and replace with water once. Milk left = 20*(1-5/20)=20*(3/4)=15 L.
mistakes: Using replaced amount in numerator incorrectly relative to current/total volume as stated
Forgetting to apply the factor repeatedly for multiple replacements
Confusing amount removed with amount remaining
